sources_considered.why: Primary longitudinal measurements end in April 2024, although publication occurred in July.
Primary analysis distinguishes growing data stocks from even faster growth in training-data demand.
The current abstract reflects a revised forecast. The dated 2022 Epoch analysis was used to avoid conflating versions.

evidence_items.locator: Section 3.1, The Decline of Consent to Open Web Data

receipt.public_excerpt: Robots.txt crawling restrictions have risen precipitously since mid-2023.

evidence_items.explanation: Measurements ending in April 2024 show increased restrictions on sources represented in three web-text corpora. This supports a narrower claim about access to existing sources, but does not establish a net decline in all remaining usable training data.

Epoch's exhaustion argument compares demand growth with growing data stocks and acknowledges substantial uncertainty. This is counterevidence to treating an exhaustion forecast as proof that the stock itself was shrinking, but it does not measure April 2024 availability.

unresolved_gaps: No comprehensive April 2024 inventory of remaining usable training material was found.
The restriction study measures access conditions for existing web sources, not net supply after new content, licensing, reuse and synthetic generation.
The evidence does not establish an aggregate decline across text, image and video data.
